raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
`minimax_h3_time_shift_sigmas(num_steps=N)` currently returns `N` sigma points, but the H3 denoise loop executes `len(sigmas) - 1` transitions. A 1-step request therefore fails admission, and every larger request performs one fewer denoise update than requested.

This change builds `N + 1` sigma endpoints and adds coverage for 1, 2, 10, and 50 requested steps with both H3 video and audio shift scales.

Validation:

- `PYTHONPATH=.pytest-deps:python .../python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_denoise_loop.py` — 5 passed.
- H200 end-to-end smoke: 1 requested step executed `1/1` denoise update and produced a 1344×768, 124-frame H.264 video with AAC audio.

Addressed the three review findings in cf296772db6: one-step requests now pass admission, online AdaLN capacity is checked against N plans, and warmup workload accounting reports N denoising iterations. Also migrated the shared FastH3/VDN and PDD consumers to transition counts while preserving their trained sigma grids (4/8 forwards, 5/9 grid points), and updated offline AdaLN/PDD configuration and documentation. Existing PDD fused configuration must be regenerated with the updated fusion tool; mismatched head counts fail closed.

Validation: the registered CUDA regression entry point passed all 28 cases, and the six existing related test files passed all 91 tests. The same new boundary tests reproduced eight failures against the pre-fix main-merged branch. Pre-commit, documentation build validation, and broken-link checks passed. These tests exercise real admission, timestep preparation, CUDA scheduler updates and fusion/config loading; expensive DiT computation is replaced in the loop test, so this is not a claim of full-model generation or GT/performance validation. New-head CI remains to be verified. Thanks for the original fix and the review findings!

Validated the step-count change before refreshing GT:

- Compared against Diffusers' MiniMaxH3Scheduler at `d961a388fd02e4db38d17350c8dd9b8abe642e05`: 18 CUDA combinations (1/2/7/8/10/50 updates, shifts 3/6/12). Sigma grids and every Euler update are bitwise equal, max error 0. The reference counts sigma points; N updates need N+1 points.
- Ran real H3 FL2VA on H200 (4s, 672x384, seed 42, 8 updates), with native grids, independently generated reference grids, and a native repeat. All 107 video frames are pixel-identical. Reference-grid audio is bitwise equal to native-repeat audio; both differ from the first request by max 1.93e-7, RMSE 1.82e-8. This compares schedules within the native engine, not two independent full pipelines.
- Traced both previous H100 GT sources: T2VA used the old 8-point grid; Ref2VA's [GT-generation log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36597643222/job/109506691186) explicitly shows request=8 but `7/7` updates. New CI outputs execute `8/8`; both requests produce byte-identical three-frame PNGs for each case.

Updated only six H100 video PNGs plus provenance in [ci-data-diffusion](https://github.com/sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion/commit/a94acbdf8c5442c39f7c0cfce7da2f03768be8e5). No audio GT, official GT, or thresholds were changed. H200 outputs were not used as H100 GT. T2VA uses run 37658908853 because the newest run skipped that partition; Ref2VA uses run 37765026897.

Also added a closed-form grid assertion, documented the migration, and changed the remaining FastH3/VDN CI requests from 9 to 8. Focused tests: 102 passed + 6 subtests; pre-commit passed.

Verified the new remote GT pin through the real resolver (no local GT override): both requests of both H100 cases pass the unchanged thresholds, with SSIM=1 and mean absolute difference=0. This verifies artifact/pin alignment; fresh CI is still required to check newly generated outputs.

### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `4657114514`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
[Your team has set up Codex to review pull requests in this repo](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/general). Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow one-step schedules through pipeline admission**

When `num_inference_steps=1`, this now correctly produces two endpoints and one denoise transition, but `MiniMaxH3PartitionAdmissionStage.forward` still rejects every request below 2, and that stage is installed by `MiniMaxH3Pipeline`. Consequently the public serving path still cannot use the newly supported one-step schedule; update the admission threshold and its endpoint-based error message.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for the extra AdaLN plan in admission**

With online AdaLN enabled, a request whose `num_inference_steps` is one greater than `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_ADALN_GPU_PLANS` is still admitted because `release_metadata.py` checks `num_inference_steps - 1 > gpu_plans`. This change makes the denoise loop prepare `num_inference_steps` timestep plans, so `MiniMaxH3AdalnCache` later raises after the expensive encoding stages because the slab is one slot short; the admission calculation and diagnostic must use the new transition count.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update warmup iteration accounting for N transitions**

During auto-residency warmup, `MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage.default_workload_iterations` still reports `max(1, num_inference_steps - 1)` even though this schedule now executes exactly `num_inference_steps` transitions. Those reported counts are used to extrapolate the full-workload denoising duration and layer-use counts, so H3 placement estimates remain off by one step and can be badly skewed for short calibration requests; update the formula alongside the schedule cardinality.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+            request = _request(steps)
+            assert admission.forward(request, server_args) is request
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="9 AdaLN plans.*slab holds 8"):
+            admission.forward(_request(9), server_args)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "params_class,steps", [(FastH3SamplingParams, 8), (VDNH3SamplingParams, 8)]
+)
+def test_distilled_models_keep_their_trained_grid(params_class, steps):
+    request = Req(sampling_params=params_class(prompt="step contract"))
+    assert request.num_inference_steps == steps
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        params_class(prompt="step contract", num_inference_steps=steps + 1)
+
+
+def test_fasth3_trained_rungs_preserve_serving_and_warmup_counts(admission):
+    sampling = FastH3SamplingParams(
+        prompt="step contract",
+        task="t2va",
+        conditions=[],
+        target={"short_edge": 768, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "duration_seconds": 5.0},
+        flow_shift=10.0,
+        audio_flow_shift=3.0,
+    )
+    request = Req(sampling_params=sampling, extra=sampling.build_request_extra())
+    admission.forward(request, SimpleNamespace(minimax_h3_adaln_online=False))
+    preparation = MiniMaxH3TimestepPreparationStage(
+        dmd_denoising_steps=(999, 874, 749, 624, 500, 375, 250, 125)
+    )
+    warmup_requests = [request.copy_as_warmup(steps) for steps in (1, 2, 8)]
+    preparation.forward(request, SimpleNamespace())
+    assert len(request.timesteps) == 8
+    assert all(
+        len(schedule) == 9 and schedule[-1] == 0.0
+        for schedule in request.extra[MINIMAX_H3_SIGMAS_EXTRA_KEY].values()
+    )
+    for steps, warmup in zip((1, 2, 8), warmup_requests):
+        preparation.forward(warmup, SimpleNamespace())
+        assert len(warmup.timesteps) == steps
+        for modality, schedule in warmup.extra[MINIMAX_H3_SIGMAS_EXTRA_KEY].items():
+            assert (
+                schedule
+                == request.extra[MINIMAX_H3_SIGMAS_EXTRA_KEY][modality][: steps + 1]
+            )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("steps", [1, 2, 10, 50])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "mode", ["t2va", "fl2va", "ref2va-image", "ref2va-audio", "ref2va-mixed"]
+)
+def test_offline_adaln_builder_prepares_one_plan_per_transition(steps, mode):
+    plans = build_minimax_h3_adaln_cache._cache_timestep_plans(
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            timesteps=None,
+            num_inference_steps=steps,
+            flow_shift=12.0,
+            audio_flow_shift=3.0,
+            imgvid_cond_noise_aug=0.999,
+            audio_cond_noise_aug=1.0,
+            mode=mode,
+        )
+    )
+    assert len(plans) == steps
+    assert all(plan.numel() > 0 for plan in plans)
+
+
+def test_fused_pdd_config_and_warmup_match_head_count(tmp_path, admission):
+    heads = {
+        name: torch.ones(32, 2, 3) if name.endswith("weight") else torch.ones(32, 2)
+        for name in (
+            "proj_out.weight",
+            "proj_out.bias",
+            "audio_proj_out.weight",
+            "audio_proj_out.bias",
+        )
+    }
+    save_file(heads, tmp_path / "pdd_heads.safetensors")
+    config_path = tmp_path / "pdd_config.json"
+    config_path.write_text(json.dumps({"num_steps": 32, "block_size": 4}))
+    with patch.object(sys, "argv", ["fuse_minimax_h3_pdd_heads", str(tmp_path)]):
+        assert fuse_minimax_h3_pdd_heads.main() == 0
+    config = json.loads(config_path.read_text())
+    assert config["fused_steps"] == config["num_inference_steps"] == 8
+    with patch.dict(
+        os.environ,
+        {
+            "SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_PDD_HEADS": str(
+                tmp_path / "pdd_fused_heads.safetensors"
+            )
+        },
+    ):
+        preparation = MiniMaxH3TimestepPreparationStage()
+    serving = _request(8)
+    admission.forward(serving, SimpleNamespace(minimax_h3_adaln_online=False))
+    preparation.forward(serving, SimpleNamespace())
+    for steps in (1, 2, 8):
+        warmup = serving.copy_as_warmup(steps)
+        preparation.forward(warmup, SimpleNamespace())
+        assert len(warmup.timesteps) == steps
+        for modality, schedule in warmup.extra[MINIMAX_H3_SIGMAS_EXTRA_KEY].items():
+            assert (
+                schedule
+                == serving.extra[MINIMAX_H3_SIGMAS_EXTRA_KEY][modality][: steps + 1]
+            )
+
+    config["num_inference_steps"] = 9
+    config_path.write_text(json.dumps(config))
+    with patch.dict(
+        os.environ,
+        {
+            "SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_PDD_HEADS": str(
+                tmp_path / "pdd_fused_heads.safetensors"
+            )
+        },
+    ):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="config does not match the fused heads"):
+            MiniMaxH3TimestepPreparationStage()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow one-step schedules through pipeline admission**

When `num_inference_steps=1`, this now correctly produces two endpoints and one denoise transition, but `MiniMaxH3PartitionAdmissionStage.forward` still rejects every request below 2, and that stage is installed by `MiniMaxH3Pipeline`. Consequently the public serving path still cannot use the newly supported one-step schedule; update the admission threshold and its endpoint-based error message.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for the extra AdaLN plan in admission**

With online AdaLN enabled, a request whose `num_inference_steps` is one greater than `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_ADALN_GPU_PLANS` is still admitted because `release_metadata.py` checks `num_inference_steps - 1 > gpu_plans`. This change makes the denoise loop prepare `num_inference_steps` timestep plans, so `MiniMaxH3AdalnCache` later raises after the expensive encoding stages because the slab is one slot short; the admission calculation and diagnostic must use the new transition count.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update warmup iteration accounting for N transitions**

During auto-residency warmup, `MiniMaxH3DenoisingStage.default_workload_iterations` still reports `max(1, num_inference_steps - 1)` even though this schedule now executes exactly `num_inference_steps` transitions. Those reported counts are used to extrapolate the full-workload denoising duration and layer-use counts, so H3 placement estimates remain off by one step and can be badly skewed for short calibration requests; update the formula alongside the schedule cardinality.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
